file.excelNote: Excel files are read into memory as a whole; for large data, save as CSV first
file.ragged: {{count}} rows have a different number of columns from the header (extra ignored, missing as NULL).
file.badEncoding: {{count}} cells have characters that could not be decoded; check the encoding.
file.errorCells: {{count}} error values (such as #N/A) will be imported as NULL.

target.badCells: {{count}} values in the preview cannot be converted to this column's type, e.g. {{first}}

upsertBlocked.no_key: The table has no primary key
upsertBlocked.key_unmapped: Not all primary key columns are mapped

options.replaceWarn: All rows in the table will be deleted (DELETE, in the same transaction as the import and rolled back on failure; slow for large tables)
options.mysqlUpsert: MySQL family: any unique key conflict leads to an update, not only the primary key
options.wholeNote: Any failed row rolls back everything
options.stopNote: On error, the failing batch is rolled back and the import stops; earlier batches stay committed
options.skipNote: On error, the failing batch is retried row by row; failed rows go to the error report, others are written
options.prodNote: This is a production connection; you will be asked to confirm before starting
options.prodContent: Rows will be imported into {{table}} with "{{mode}}".

result.warnings: {{count}} warnings (column count mismatch, decoding failure or error values)

sql.title: Run SQL File
sql.transaction: One transaction (commit only if all succeed)
sql.transactionNote: Stops and rolls back on error. DDL in MySQL, Oracle and DM commits implicitly and cannot be rolled back; the file should not contain its own transaction statements.
sql.scanNote: The whole file is scanned first: statements are counted and those needing confirmation (such as DROP or DELETE without WHERE) are checked.
sql.prodNote: This is a production connection; after scanning, the statement count and risky statements are listed for confirmation
sql.confirmContent: The file has {{total}} statements. These need confirmation:
sql.confirmMore: {{count}} more statements needing confirmation are not listed
sql.moreInLog: Only the first 100 are listed; see the log for the rest
